newsitem.title: CANADA: Rogers sets shopping pact, seeks partners.
newsitem.headline: Rogers sets shopping pact, seeks partners.

text.p: Rogers Communications Inc said on Friday it signed a pact with Comcast Corp unit QVC Inc to pursue a televised home shopping venture in Canada.
Rogers Broadcasting currently carries on televised shopping through the Shopping Channel.

"Rogers' alliance with QVC not only reflects our focus on maximizing the potential value of these assets, but also underscores our attraction as a strategic partner for other major players," said Rogers chief executive Ted Rogers in a statement.
"We continue to look for additional partners to expand the growth opportunities in both cable and telecommunications," Ted Rogers added.
Rogers said in the past few days he has bought one million Rogers shares for his own account, bringing the total amount he has purchased this year to two million shares.
He said Rogers continues to focus on cutting the debt load at its cable unit.
The company is still committed to lowering the debt-to-EBITDA (earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization) ratio to near industry standards.
Rogers plans to accomplish this de-leveraging process through a variety of measures.

The first will be an equity infusion into the cable operation during 1996 of more than C$600 million. Of that total, C$250 million will come from the sale proceeds from Toronto Sun in which RCI holds a 63 percent interest.
Rogers will also cut capital expenditures and refocused on that spending which produces more immediate financial returns.
The company said it will combine revenue growth from new products with cost-cutting to improve operating margins and enhance operating performance at Rogers Cablesystems.
Rogers chief financial officer Graham Savage resigned suddenly this week, the second top-tier executive to leave the company this year.
The QVC joint venture is subject to the execution of a definitive agreement and approval of the respective boards which is expected by September 30.

The venture will be dubbed QVC Co and will be licensed exclusively to use the QVC trademarks in Canada for the televised home shopping business. The parties will also cooperate to take advantage of further economies of scale and to secure volume purchasing discounts, the companies said.
Rogers will maintain management and voting control of the new enterprise.
